headline: Rivian's chief executive says the carmaker's vehicles will in future run AI agents from other companies such as Anthropic, with no date given.
score_reason: Statement of intent at an event with no timing or product details.
importance_line: Rivian drivers may eventually talk to outside assistants in the car, but only for convenience features: the chief executive says vehicle controls such as braking and steering will not be handed to an agent.
summary: TechCrunch reports that RJ Scaringe, Rivian's founder and chief executive, said at TechCrunch Disrupt that Rivian's cars will in future be able to run AI agents made by companies such as Anthropic, though he gave no date and the company pointed to its AI and Autonomy Day in December. Scaringe said vehicle-level controls like braking and steering will not be handed to an agent, and that the work needs a lot of plumbing and coordination with the AI labs.
